result:
`Nota final > 6` should now be true when the consolidation value is `10`. I haven't run any tests or tried it in the app.

The fix is in `app/models/admissions/form_condition.rb`. Consolidation fields are `CODE` or `EMAIL`, so `get_type` reports them as `"string"`. The `>=`, `<=`, `>` and `<` comparisons therefore compared them as strings.

I added a helper, `comparison_type`, that these four operators now use. When a field is typed as a string but both the field value and the condition value parse as numbers, it compares them as numbers. The parsing accepts a comma as the decimal separator. If either side isn't numeric, the comparison stays a string comparison, so text fields behave as before.

One consequence to be aware of: this applies to any string-typed field, not only consolidation fields. A text field that holds `10` compared against `6` will now also be compared numerically.
